name: Porsche 911 (964) floor pan and body datum frame, steel

coordinate_system.origin: plane of symmetry, vertically above the front axle center, on the nominal ground plane
coordinate_system.axes: X forward, Y to the left, Z up
coordinate_system.vehicle_transform_note: established by fitting the plane of symmetry to the scan: yaw -2.236 deg, roll -0.451 deg, centerline at X_scan +112.0 mm; ground taken at the mean contact of the four tires
coordinate_system.vehicle_transform_provenance: Row-major 4x4 homogeneous matrix that maps raw scan coordinates to the ADR-0003 vehicle frame. Composed from frame_params.npy: lateral recentering, yaw cancellation, roll cancellation, then axis permutation and origin shift. VERIFIED end to end — applied to 200,000 vertices drawn at random from the scan, it reproduces verts_vehicle.npy with a maximum error of 1.3e-4 mm.

sheet_thickness_mm.provenance: values reported by the project owner, not found in the volume V read here
sheet_thickness_mm.note: Unexplained 0.2 mm discrepancy. Hot-dip galvanized body shell: zinc, primer, paint and wax add to the sheet, so a measurement on a fitted panel measures the stack, not the steel. The analysis uses 0.8 mm; using 1.0 would overstate stiffness by 25%.

materials.note: Volume V names the six high-strength steel panels but publishes neither grade nor thickness. The density of 7.85e-6 kg/mm3 used for the mass is a generic steel value, not manufacturer data. German-language search of 2026-09-03: the hot-dip galvanizing process is confirmed by a primary Porsche source, but NO public source, German or otherwise, publishes a sheet thickness in mm, a zinc mass per m2 or a steel grade for the 964. The 0.2 mm discrepancy therefore remains unexplained and the 0.8 mm analysis remains the defensible choice.
materials.process: sheet steel hot-dip galvanized on both sides (feuerverzinkt), entire body-in-white since model year 1981, documented by Porsche; see SRC-PORSCHE-GALVANISED-BODY-911

interfaces.acceptance_rule: each control dimension recomputed on the model must fall within the tolerance published in 50-03, left/right difference included
at least one published datum point must be locatable on the scan to better than its tolerance

checks_passed: Scan scale: measured wheelbase 2278.1 mm against 2272 mm factory, i.e. +0.27%. The mesh is in millimeters at 1:1 scale.

Frame: after yaw correction, the left/right offset of the wheel centers drops from 66.7 to 12.7 mm at the front and from 51.1 to 5.3 mm at the rear, although the wheels do not enter the plane-of-symmetry fit.

Dimensioning scheme: the cross diagonal M recomputes to 1787.8 mm from the published E, F and R, against 1788 +/- 3 mm in the manual, a 0.2 mm difference. A purely documentary check, independent of the scan.

CalculiX torsion test: stiffness follows thickness linearly (ratio 1.251 for 1.250), hence a box section in membrane shear. The 1% most loaded nodes are 100% in the side rail, including after excluding 300 mm around the clamped end, which corroborates the HS steel choice of plate 50-013 for the inner side member.

A convergence worth noting, without over-interpreting it: the analysis places the torsional load path in the side rail, plate 50-013 puts high-strength steel there, and German buying guides name the sill jacking point as a recurring corrosion hotspot. It follows that, FOR EQUAL CORROSION, an attack at the jacking point has more structural consequence than elsewhere on the floor pan. This reasoning is about consequence, not frequency: no source documents a structural failure at that location.

Scale robustness tested. The wheel components are covered over 360 degrees, not over a partial arc. Forcing the radius to diameters of 560 to 680 mm, the derived wheelbase stays between 2270.4 and 2278.9 mm, i.e. 2272 +/- 7. The scale check therefore does not depend on the tire radius estimate, which itself is unstable.

Composite material study on the same torsion test, geometry and loading unchanged. The 0.8 mm steel reference was first reproduced identically (2442 N.m/deg) before any change. Quasi-isotropic laminate properties are computed from the ply constants through the lamination invariants, in a self-checked module: the QI stack of an isotropic ply returns that ply. QI carbon comes out at E = 52,401 MPa, a handbook value for a QI T300/epoxy. At equal stiffness: monolithic carbon 0.82x the areal mass of steel, 50/50 carbon/aramid hybrid 0.99x, aramid 1.30x. The thickness predicted by the G*t law is confirmed by the full analysis to within 6.9%, which extends to the material the membrane scaling law already established for thickness.

Third scale check, independent of the wheels and of the manual: the overall length of the scan in the vehicle frame is 4282.4 mm against 4275 mm in the 964 catalog, i.e. +7.4 mm or +0.17%. Same sign and same order of magnitude as the +0.27% wheelbase difference. It anchors nothing in X, since the extremities are bumper skins and not reference planes.

The 964 underbody is FLAT: there is no center tunnel. The relief between the median Z at |Y| < 60 mm and that of the sides at 250 < |Y| < 400 mm is -0.7 to -3.1 mm over eight stations spanning 1000 mm, less than the scan symmetry residual of 7.54 mm RMS. Consistent with a rear engine and the absence of a longitudinal shaft. See source/tunnel_probe.py.

Independent cross-check of dimension R from volume V: a 993 thread reports 1245 mm between the front and rear jacking points, against R = 1245 +/- 2 mm published between P17 and P18 for the 964. A non-Porsche source therefore reproduces the transcription, and the 964 and 993 share the longitudinal spacing of the jacking points. See SRC-RENNLIST-993-JACKING-POINT-DISCREPANCY.

Architecture versus material, at equal mass, on the same test: closing the body shell gives x 1.51 in specific stiffness, switching to carbon x 1.25, and the two multiply (1.86 measured for 1.89 expected), so the levers are separable. The floor-pan-only case reproduces exactly the mesh and the 2442 N.m/deg value of the original model.

Defect found by a connectivity check added to the mesh builder: the rear crossmember of the datum network, placed at x = -1703, fell behind the rear edge of the modeled floor pan at x = -1500 and formed a floating island. It accounted for 0.264 m2 and 1.66 kg, i.e. 5.7% of the model mass, for zero contribution to stiffness. Check: with the original geometry, removing it returns exactly 2442 N.m/deg, the published value. The published stiffnesses were therefore correct; the masses, and hence all specific stiffnesses K/m, were understated. The crossmember was removed rather than reattached, because it sits behind the clamped section of the test and could carry nothing even if connected. The CAD model floor_assembly.py is not affected: it produces an assembly of separate solids, where a crossmember placed on an unanchored datum point is a documented state and not a defect.

Shell model extended from the floor pan alone to a closed cell (wheel arches, B-pillars, roof rails, roof, windshield frame): K x 3.7 for mass x 2.3. The usable result is the ranking, not the values. The windshield frame, 1.1 kg, brings the largest increment of the whole ladder, while the roof, 10.5 kg, brings only +1%, and the B-pillars and roof rails added alone bring nothing for 7.5 kg because they do not close the ring at the front. Topological hypothesis tested and not merely asserted: ring_study.py adds the roof and the windshield frame separately to the same open cage, at three mesh densities. The per-kilogram efficiency ratio stays at two orders of magnitude (191x, 172x, 191x) while the absolute stiffness drifts by 11%, and the two elements together return 1.6 times the sum of their separate contributions, which is the same claim seen from the other side.

Laminated CalculiX chain established and validated: *SHELL SECTION, COMPOSITE with one *ORIENTATION per ply and per panel family. Validation on an analytical case of uniaxial tension on a unidirectional ply: E_x = 130,516 MPa at 0 degrees for E1 = 135,000 expected, 9,909 at 90 degrees for E2 = 10,000, and 13,080 at 45 degrees for 13,200 predicted off-axis, i.e. 3% at worst. Three undocumented constraints resolved: COMPOSITE requires quadratic S6 or S8R shells, the 4th field of a layer is an orientation name and not an angle, and OUTPUT=2D is ignored because the .frd carries the expanded 3D model.

Load-carrying mechanism measured, no longer assumed. dominance_study.py varies E and G separately by means of a fictitious orthotropic material with decoupled moduli. Floor pan alone: doubling E gives +93.8%, doubling G gives +2.1% — the structure works in BENDING, not in shear. Closed cell: +37.7% and +56.9% — shear becomes dominant without being exclusive. Closing a ring therefore does not merely add stiffness, it changes the mechanism that carries it. Corollary verified by a full laminate analysis: the ranking of layups reverses with the architecture. Floor pan alone 0/90 1910, QI 1586, +/-45 696; closed cell +/-45 6849, QI 6311, 0/90 4043.

Longitudinal chain closed from published dimensions (datum_chain_50_05a.py). Plate 50-05a gives three stations from the 0 line through the front strut mounts P4: P1 722 +/- 2 ahead, P3 215 ahead, P5 143 +/- 2 behind. Plate 50-02 draws P as a longitudinal dimension, not a diagonal. P17 then comes out at 441.1 mm behind the 0 line through P5-P20-K and at 439.2 mm through P3-L: two independent published paths agree within 1.9 mm, against a 3.6 mm tolerance spread.

The published chain is tied to the scan (scan_tie_50_05a.py): the P5 bosses are found at |Y| = 385.2 and 386.9 mm against 385 published, the P17 receptacles and the P19 pads nearby. Six features give the 0 line at delta = -25.5 mm in the vehicle frame (spread 7.2 mm, +/- 7.6 mm with the wheel-centre fit): behind the front wheel centres, as a strut-mount line is with the 4 deg 25 min caster of volume IV.
known_limits: The longitudinal anchoring is resolved for P20, P3, P5, P17, P18 and P19 from published dimensions; its tie to the scan's wheel frame carries +/- 7.6 mm (delta = -25.5 mm). The earlier registration test (16/16 points within 2.8 mm of structure) proved nothing, since random points did as well; it is superseded by scan_tie_50_05a.py, which measures identified features.

P12 and P21 hang on diagonals N and O, whose crossed-plan reading is not decoded: it places P12 73 mm ahead of the transmission cross-member bosses measured on the scan. P12 is carried as a scan measurement; P21, at X = -3072 mm under the same reading, lands in the rear engine-carrier cross-member band, not in the bumper, but stays invalid.

The 0 line of plate 50-05a is read as the line through the front strut mounts, as drawn; the plates do not name it. The scan tie supports that reading (it lies 25.5 mm behind the wheel centres), but a direct published definition was not found.

The scan is a wide body that does not match the original: rear track measured at about 1459 mm against 1374 mm factory. The widened fenders and sills are not production 964 geometry; only the floor pan and the central structure are usable as a reference.
The ground plane is the weakest datum: derived from the contact of the four tires, it shows a 55 mm scatter. Every Z dimension carries this uncertainty.

The side rail and crossmember sections, and the sheet thickness, are not published in volume V: they are working values declared ASSUMED in the script. The 36.8 kg mass covers only the modeled solids and is not a body shell mass.
The scan symmetry residual is 7.54 mm RMS. Part of it is real, since a 911 underside is asymmetric, but no interface can be declared measured to better than this order of magnitude.
No physical check: in accordance with the charter, nothing was weighed or measured on a vehicle.

The computed torsional stiffness, 2442 N.m/deg at 0.8 mm, applies only to the modeled solids: floor pan, two side rails, two crossmembers. It is not the stiffness of a 964 body shell and must not be quoted as such. Nor are the more complete variants of the shell model, up to 9093 N.m/deg for the closed cell: their pillar, roof rail and B-pillar sections and their roof height are all ASSUMED, and the model has no bonded glazing, no doors and no openings in the panels, which acts precisely in the direction that flatters the closed ring.

German-language search: no published torsional stiffness was found for the 964, whatever the variant. The computed 2442 N.m/deg therefore has no factory value to be checked against, in either direction.

The grade of the six high-strength steel panels of plate 50-013 remains unknown: no public source gives it. The analysis uses only a generic steel with E = 210,000 MPa, valid for stiffness but not for a margin to the yield strength.

The longitudinal anchoring has one identified but closed lead: Celette sells under reference 564.320 a 964-specific jig set advertised with 42 control points, but all of its documentation sits behind authentication. See SRC-CELETTE-564-320-964-JIG. The realistic route goes through a body shop subscribed to Car-O-Data or equipped with Celette, not through a public source.

Volume IV provides two vertical dimensions referenced to the ground: the front body point "Crossmember to body", which is P5, at 165 +/- 10 mm, and the outer rear-arm mounting on the body side at 270 +/- 5 mm, for a Carrera 2/4 at DIN 70020 curb weight. They are not yet used to check the scan ground plane: that requires locating these mountings on the mesh and knowing the ride height of the scanned vehicle, which is a wide body that has probably been modified. A measured difference would indicate lowering, not a frame error.

The composite study covers ONLY stiffness. It says nothing about laminate strength, delamination, bonded joints — a real weak point of a composite monocoque —, buckling, crash, fire, fatigue or aging; a composite failure criterion is not a von Mises stress. The ply constants are handbook-class, evidence level D, not supplier-certified, and the cured ply thickness of 0.25 mm is ASSUMED. The real gain of a monocoque is architectural and cannot be demonstrated on a floor pan alone. CORRECTION of 2026-09-04: the interpretation of this study as a G/rho criterion was wrong. The separate sensitivity measurement shows that the floor pan alone works in bending, so its criterion is E/rho. The computed values remain valid, since they all concern isotropic materials where E and G are proportional; it is their mechanical reading that is corrected. The ranking of carbon ahead of aramid is not affected.

A replacement self-supporting structure carries occupant restraint: classified prohibited_pending_engineering in the sense of SAFETY.md. No part geometry or layup sequence can be released, and the ZESAD record publishes no mass, stiffness, crash test, homologation, layup or core material, so nothing in it can be compared against.

The "tunnel" case of the architecture study, which carries the largest gain in the dossier (+71%), is NOT 964 geometry: the scan shows a flat underbody. It quantifies a possible architectural modification, not an existing part. It is also the most actionable conclusion: adding a closed longitudinal beam returns more than switching to carbon, +71% against +25%.

No published torsional stiffness of a 964 body shell was found, including by a targeted German-language search of 2026-09-04 on Verwindungssteifigkeit and Torsionssteifigkeit. The only figure encountered, about 11,563 N.m/deg, is a forum aggregate with no primary source or protocol, not even stating whether it refers to a body-in-white or a complete vehicle. It is recorded for the record only and MUST NOT be used as a reference. See SRC-RENNLIST-911-TORSIONAL-RIGIDITY-LIST.

The shell model is not mesh-converged. The absolute stiffness still drops by 4% at the last refinement tried, the S3 elements converging from above. Only the ratios between architectures, verified at three mesh densities, are usable; no absolute value is.

Crash is the only software blocker of the monocoque program: CalculiX is an implicit solver and handles neither large-deformation impact, nor laminate failure, nor delamination. No crashworthiness claim can come out of this chain. See docs/MONOCOQUE_964_993_CHAINE_CALCUL.md.
